A safe stop was possible when amber was first observed: stop before the line and wait for green. Car `challenge_tailgater` is tailgating the car, 8 m behind (0.7 s): far too close to stop if the car brakes suddenly. Never brake-check it, and never brake harder than 3 m/s^2 unless something ahead calls for more (the amber light ahead needs 1.9 m/s^2); never speed up to please it either. Leave twice the usual gap to whatever is ahead (`car.target_speed` already does), so the car can brake early and gently. There is no lane to move right into: ease off a little, gently (`ease_off_for_tailgater`, where it is offered), so it can pass when it is safe. Objects beyond 80 m or behind buildings are unseen; an empty traffic list does not prove the road is clear. Choose the maneuver for the next second using driving_style and the visible situation. The 3-second predictions have passed collision and road-rule checks against observed objects only; unseen objects and later changes remain possible. Weigh progress against braking, cornering, nearby clearance, roadside activity and limited sight lines. car.target_speed is a planning reference for limits, curves and stopping room, not a required choice. You may slow earlier or choose a safe lateral clearance when the situation or style warrants it. Keep moving when there is adequate visible room; hold still only for a present obstruction or a required stop at the car's current position.
